stage1.impression: A warm brick-and-records den with a red translucent speaker on a pale plinth, but everything is the same orange, so the 'only colour in the room' gets lost: the speaker reads as a dark maroon plastic box, darker than the brick behind it. The brick is a flat, visibly repeating photo texture, the chair and rug are smooth CG surfaces, and the plinth sits on the rug with almost no weight. It reads as a competent arch-viz render, not a magazine interior.

blocking_9: The Ember speaker must be the brightest saturated object in the frame and read as tinted, lit-through acrylic with the white batts visible, not as a dark maroon box (cabinet lum_median >= 55 while the brick behind it is lower)
The brick must read as real, non-repeating masonry with mortar depth, and it must not out-shine the hero
The grade must separate the speaker's red from the room's amber: the walls are currently b_median 30 / 23, monochrome orange
The sconce shade must not clip (42.7% clipped now)
The plinth needs a visible contact shadow and the rug needs pile, so the speaker has weight on the floor
The leather chair and the rug need real material micro-detail (grain, wear, fibre) instead of smooth CG shading

defects.what: The brick texture tiles visibly (repeating brick patterns and identical chipped faces), with no mortar relief. It reads as wallpaper, and the corner seam at x~630 shows two textures with the same pattern.
The horn reads as a dark red slab with a black hole and a streaky specular. It sits on thin posts above the cabinet and looks detached.
The cabinet is darker (lum_median 27) than the wall behind it (80-91). The red goes almost black and the white batts don't read.
The sconce shade is blown: 42.7% clipped, a flat white blob with no glow structure.
The leather chair is smooth and plasticky with no grain, seams or wear, and the frame edge crops it awkwardly.
The rug is a flat grey-brown plane with no pile or fibre, and the plinth casts almost no shadow on it.
The record wall's spines are bright and busy (p95 147) and pull the eye from the speaker. The spines repeat.
The amp/stand-in on the console is a black box with two flat glowing rectangles and reads as a placeholder.
The whole frame is one amber hue (blue channel 10-30 everywhere), so there is no colour hierarchy and no depth separation.

changes.problem: The hero speaker is darker than its background, so the tinted acrylic doesn't glow and the batts don't read.

evidence.measured: cabinet lum_median 27.4, r 56 / g 14 / b 1, against the brick wall's lum_median 91.3 and the right wall's 79.7

change.setting: lamps: on each Ember speaker 2 x area, W/m2 at the target
change.to: 10.0 W/m2, 3200 K, one aimed from upper camera-left to rake the front baffle and one behind/inside to backlight the acrylic

changes.expected: The cabinet glows red-through and the white batts show as pale pink shapes behind the tint. The cabinet becomes the brightest saturated mass in the frame.

changes.problem: The sconce over-lights the brick and its shade clips, so the wall out-shines the speaker.

evidence.measured: upper-left wall lum_median 91.3, p95 142.6. Sconce shade [300,150,350,195] clip_pct 42.7

change.setting: lamps: sconces point W; the room's glowing surfaces: sconce shades

changes.expected: The brick drops to a dim warm pool around the sconce that falls off toward the corner, and the shade shows a soft gradient instead of white.

changes.problem: The grade is monochrome amber, so the speaker's red has no colour contrast against the room.

evidence.measured: right wall r 144 / g 66 / b 23. Left wall b_median 30. Floor b_median 5-11

changes.expected: The 2400-2700 K sources still read warm but less orange. The brick goes toward a dusty terracotta-brown and the speaker's crimson separates from it.

changes.problem: The brick is a flat, visibly tiling texture with no mortar depth, which says 'render'.

evidence.measured: seen at 2x crop: identical brick faces repeat across both walls, there is no parallax or shadow in the mortar joints, and the albedo is uniform

change.to: a high-res, non-repeating old-brick set (4K+, randomised per-brick UV offset and hue variation) with displacement or a normal map, mortar recessed 4-6 mm, roughness 0.85, albedo darkened about 20% and desaturated toward sooty red-brown

changes.expected: The brick shows raking-light relief under the sconce, uneven bricks and no repeat. The wall goes darker and quieter behind the speaker.

changes.problem: The record wall is the brightest busy area and pulls the eye from the speaker.

evidence.measured: lum_p95 147.4, lum_range 130.5, the highest-contrast region in the frame

change.setting: lamps: the record wall spot W; record-wall strip emission

changes.expected: The spines read as a darker rhythmic texture in support, and the speaker leads.

changes.problem: The chair leather and the rug are smooth CG surfaces with no micro-detail.

evidence.measured: chair back [150,360,300,500] lum_median 32 with a smooth gradient and no grain. The rug shows no fibre structure at 2x

change.to: leather: cognac aniline with a pebble-grain normal map, roughness 0.45-0.65 by a wear mask, darker creases and seam piping. Rug: wool pile with a fibre normal/displacement about 6 mm and slight colour mottling

changes.expected: The chair reads as worn real leather catching the sconce in soft broken highlights, and the rug shows pile texture and soft shading.

changes.problem: The plinth hardly grounds on the rug or floor, and there is no atmosphere to carry the light pools.

evidence.measured: the profile beside the plinth's left edge is flat (55.2-56.3) with no contact darkening. The right side only falls 75 to 47 over 150 px

change.setting: haze in the room's air; the plinth's footing
change.from: haze 0.006; the plinth's base sitting on top of the rug
change.to: haze 0.012; the plinth's base sunk 3 mm into the rug's pile so the pile wraps it, and the speaker's back lamp left to throw red bounce onto the floor in front

changes.expected: A dark contact line under the plinth, a faint red bounce on the floor and rug beside it, and soft glow halos around the sconce and the speaker.

changes.problem: The composition is static: the speaker sits small and centred, and the cropped chair at left is the largest mass.

evidence.measured: the chair takes about 28% of frame width as a clipped dark mass. The speaker spans only about 230 x 470 px of 1200 x 800

change.to: 40 mm, camera pulled back about 0.5 m along x and lowered to 1.0 m, re-aimed so the speaker sits on the left-third line with the chair's arm and a sliver of seat as a soft-focus foreground at f/2.8

changes.expected: The speaker gets larger and leads the frame, the chair becomes a foreground layer that gives depth, and there is negative brick space for type on the right or above.

out_of_scope.request: Close or visually anchor the gap between the horn and the cabinet: the horn on thin posts reads as detached and floating
out_of_scope.why: It is the speaker's shape and parts, which are fixed. Lighting the posts and the horn's edge can help only partly.

out_of_scope.request: The horn's resin reads as a flat dark slab with a black hole
out_of_scope.why: The horn's shape and colour are fixed. Only the light on it (c1) can change, and the horn's shape is not a picture decision.

out_of_scope.request: Replace the amp/Cumulus stand-in on the console with a real-looking unit
out_of_scope.why: Cumulus is an EARF product and fixed. If the stand-in is meant to be temporary, swap in the real model.
